thread:
samantha: Hey sec team — putting up a PR that changes auth flow for on‑prem nodes and touches secrets handling. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8342
samantha: TL;DR: add token projection for node SA, optional envelope encryption using customer KMS, and a small egress rule for health-checks to our metrics endpoint.
samantha: Planning to merge in the 18:00 PT slot today unless there are blockers. Need a quick security sanity check on SA scopes and KMS policy.
raj: Thanks — quick Qs: is the KMS usage opt-in per-customer or on by default? Also paste the SA IAM diff?
samantha: KMS is opt-in. Default behavior unchanged. SA diff: `roles/compute.viewer` removed, replaced with a narrow `roles/storage.objectViewer` + `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` for projection. I can paste the exact diff if helpful.
jess: Are we doing envelope keys in our HSM/KMS or forwarding to customer-managed keys? If customer keys, need to confirm key import/rotation process and KMS IAM.
samantha: It's customer‑managed KMS. We add a small binding to allow the node SA to 'decrypt' via a dedicated role. Rotation will be customer responsibility; we add audit logs hooks.
emily: For on‑prem VPCs, the egress to KMS endpoints requires NAT; doc update needed for minimal egress IPs. Also, health-check egress to metrics needs to be allowed — can you enumerate destination FQDNs/ips?
samantha: Will add a section to the onprem setup docs with the minimal list: `kms.{region}.cloudprovider.com`, `metrics.redwood-internal.net`. Also adding a note about proxy configs.
marco: We should avoid granting iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator broadly. Can you scope the binding to the specific service account resource and add a conditional if the provider supports it?
samantha: Yep — current PR scopes to the exact SA resource. Adding a condition to the binding where available.
raj: Two asks before LGTM: 1) add an automated smoke test that exercises token projection against a mock KMS (can be lightweight), 2) include a short audit query example for investigators (how to find projected tokens usage).
samantha: I'll add the smoke test and a brief audit snippet this morning.
sec-bot: Security quick-check: related ticket INFSEC-1247 created. Auto-scan: no high severity secrets leaked in the tree.
jess: One more: confirm whether the projected token lifetime is <= 15m and non-reusable across nodes. If it's longer, we need rotation or revocation hooks.
samantha: Projected token TTL is 10m. Non-reusable. Adding note in PR and tests to validate TTL.
emily: If you merge during the 18:00 slot, can we gate the rollout to a single region first? deploy-bot can schedule a canary.
samantha: Yes please — single-region canary then regional ramp. deploy-bot, can you hold a canary for this PR and set a rollback on error rate spike?
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for PR #8342 at 19:00 PT in us-west-2. Rollback threshold: error rate +2.5% over baseline within 10m.
raj: Sounds good. Once the smoke test and audit snippet are in, I can do a quick code review and give formal LGTM.
samantha: Added tests and audit snippet, pushed.
raj: Reviewing now. Preliminary: small nit about log redaction but not blocking. Will comment inline.
marco: Also, make sure the onprem docs call out required SCALE limits for token cache to avoid burst failures.
samantha: Good call, I'll add a note in docs.
raj: OK — LGTM from sec after tests pass and log redaction addressed.
samantha: Thanks all — merging after the canary window if deploy is green. :thumbsup:
emily: Thx. I'll monitor the canary.
samantha: Leaving a post-merge checklist in the PR with follow-ups (rotate sample keys in staging, run audit query).
raj: Marking INFSEC-1247 as reviewed.
samantha: Closing the loop here. Appreciate the quick turn.
